Type something. Anything.

Sky is built to disappear. Every decision — aperture width, terminal angle, the weight of a curve where it meets a stem — optimizes for one thing: the reader forgetting they're reading a typeface at all. Line-height matters here as much as any single letterform. Text set too tight fights the eye on every line break; text given real room to breathe lets you read for longer without noticing the effort. This paragraph is set at Sky's actual shipped default spacing — 1.45 times the type size — chosen specifically for sustained reading rather than interface density.

A typeface earns trust in exactly this kind of moment: not in a single dramatic headline, but in the fifth paragraph of a long article, when the reader hasn't stopped to think about the font at all. That's the only compliment this project is actually after.

Design philosophy

Sky is built to disappear. Every decision — aperture width, terminal angle, the weight of a curve where it meets a stem — optimizes for one thing: the reader forgetting they're reading a typeface at all.

It draws from three sources. Helvetica's structural neutrality. Frutiger's open apertures, engineered for legibility at a distance. Roboto's discipline for surviving real screens, real hinting, real rendering conditions — not just a specimen PDF.

The goal was never to be noticed. It was to be read.

Where Sky actually comes from

v0.1 is a verified foundation, not yet an original typeface. It's built on Roboto's real, professionally-drawn outlines (Copyright Google Inc., Apache License 2.0), renamed and checked glyph-by-glyph against Sky's own design specification. That verification found Roboto's actual construction already meets or exceeds most of Sky's targets — a real, useful starting point, not a shortcut we're hiding.

Some letters now carry genuine, verified modifications from that foundation — corner-softening on the straight-stemmed capitals, for a start. The plan from here is to make Sky fully original, one glyph at a time, with every change documented and nothing shipped unverified. See the roadmap for exactly where things stand.

Recent work

  • Default line-height increased to 1.45x — baked into ascent/descent metrics (not lineGap, which renders inconsistently across platforms) for sustained reading comfort.
  • Fixed asymmetric overshoot on lowercase o/c/e/s — these sat flush at x-height with zero top overshoot while correctly overshooting the baseline, making them read as optically smaller than flat letters. Now symmetric, matching the capitals.
  • ~3.2% narrower spacing — a deliberate design choice toward a quieter reading rhythm, via proportional side-bearing tightening (never by compressing letterforms).
  • Corner-softening on 24 letters + 3 digits, verified individually before shipping.
